title: FluencyCraft Advanced - Day 13
why_important: Handling crisis communications protects company reputation.

questions.question: Day 13 Practice (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 3)): When talking about inquiring about doctor appointment (every morning), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'The store vendor'?

options.a: I am inquiring about doctor appointment right now.
options.b: I need to consult a doctor regarding a mild fever.
options.c: Doctor meeting wanted for fever.
options.d: Doctor meeting wanted for fever. yesterday

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "I need to consult a doctor regarding a mild fever.".

options.d: Could we please see the menu and order starters?

questions.question: Day 13 Practice (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 3)): When talking about tracking a package delivery (this evening), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'I'?

questions.question: Day 13 Vocabulary (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 3)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'drop by'?

options.a: Visit someone informally for a short time.
options.b: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.c: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.d: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
'drop by' means: visit someone informally for a short time. Example: "Feel free to drop by our home this evening."

questions.question: Day 13 Vocabulary (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 3)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'pick out'?

options.a: Carefully choose specific items from a group.
options.b: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.c: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.d: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
'pick out' means: carefully choose specific items from a group. Example: "Could you help me pick out the best mangos?"

questions.question: Day 13 Terms (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 3)): Choose the correct definition for the phrasal verb 'reach out to':

options.a: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.b: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.c: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.d: Contact someone for help or information.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
'reach out to' means: contact someone for help or information. Example: "I will reach out to customer support tomorrow."

questions.question: Day 13 Terms (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 3)): Choose the correct definition for the phrasal verb 'iron out':

options.a: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.b: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.

options.d: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option C
'iron out' means: resolve minor problems or details in a plan. Example: "We need one final sync to iron out contract details."

questions.question:
Day 13 Translation Scenario 1 (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 3)):

Telugu: "నాకు కొంచెం తలనొప్పిగా ఉంది, ఒక గంట సేపు రెస్ట్ తీసుకుంటాను."
(Literal attempt: "To me little headache is there, take rest one hour.")

options.a: To me little headache is there, take rest one hour.
options.b: I am needing to to me little headache is there, take rest one hour.
options.c: I have a slight headache; I'm going to rest for an hour.
options.d: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option C
Natural Version: "I have a slight headache; I'm going to rest for an hour."

Say 'I have a slight headache' instead of literal translations.

questions.question:
Day 13 Telugu Scenario 2 (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 3)):

Telugu: "నేను సాధారణంగా ఉదయం 6 గంటలకే నిద్రలేచి ఒక కప్పు టీ తాగుతాను."
(Word-by-word: "I generally in morning 6 clock wake up drink tea.")

options.a: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.b: I generally in morning 6 clock wake up drink tea.
options.c: I am needing to i generally in morning 6 clock wake up drink tea.
options.d: I usually wake up at 6:00 AM and have a cup of tea.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural Version: "I usually wake up at 6:00 AM and have a cup of tea."

Use 'have a cup of tea' and specify time as '6:00 AM'.

questions.question:
Day 13 Translation Scenario 3 (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 3)):

Telugu: "ఈ టమాటాలు కేజీ ఎంత? కొంచెం తాజావి ఏరి ఇవ్వండి."
(Literal attempt: "These tomatoes kg how much? Pick give fresh.")

options.a: I am needing to these tomatoes kg how much? pick give fresh.
options.b: These tomatoes kg how much? Pick give fresh.
options.c: How much are these tomatoes per kilo? Please pick out fresh ones for me.
options.d: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option C
Natural Version: "How much are these tomatoes per kilo? Please pick out fresh ones for me."

Use 'per kilo' for price and 'pick out' for selection.

questions.question:
Day 13 Translation Scenario 4 (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 3)):

Telugu: "ముందుగా సమస్య యొక్క మూలకారణాన్ని కనుగొనాలి."
(Literal attempt: "First problem root cause finding wanted.")

options.a: First problem root cause finding wanted.
options.b: First and foremost, we must identify the root cause of the issue.
options.c: I am needing to first problem root cause finding wanted.
options.d: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural Version: "First and foremost, we must identify the root cause of the issue."

Use 'First and foremost' and 'identify the root cause'.
